title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks rallied Wed as SpaceX/Tesla merger talk broke — SpaceX +7.8%, Tesla +3.4% — on reports the two Musk companies are exploring what would be the biggest M&A deal in history; Nasdaq +1%, Dow +360pts (+0.7%), S&P 500 +0.6%.
Markets: Netflix fell 5.3% on its slowest revenue growth in years; French 10-yr bond yields topped 5% for the first time in 24 years amid post-riot fiscal/political jitters.

Companies: Anthropic's draft IPO filing shows H1 2026 revenue surged to $16.3B (from $1.1B a year earlier) but with an $80.7B net loss, mostly fundraising-related accounting charges; compute commitments could reach $750B, pushing it to offer Blackstone 10%+ yields on $9B of junior debt.
Companies: OpenAI is expanding onto Google Cloud (via Model Garden/Marketplace), adding a third major cloud partner alongside AWS and Azure as the AI infrastructure race broadens.

Macro/Policy: Investors tell Axios Anthropic can't afford to delay its IPO — private markets can no longer fund AI's ballooning capex needs, pushing the industry toward public listings even in a jittery market.

Macro/Policy: New research (Frenos) finds top AI models can now plan cyberattacks on power grids and water systems with up to ~90% success rates in tests, raising fresh critical-infrastructure security concerns.
Macro/Policy: Earnings Thursday from Valero, Spotify, P&G and Lockheed Martin; weekly jobless claims data also due.
